patient.name: Oliver Bennett
patient.presenting_event: Fell from climbing frame onto an outstretched left hand 35 minutes ago.

history.chief_complaint: Severe swollen left elbow and inability to bend it, pain 9/10.
history.mechanism: Elbow hyperextension during a fall from play structure.
history.goal: Pain relief and safe return to normal play

inspection: Anterior elbow bruising without open skin
movement: Child able to flex thumb IP and index DIP, extend thumb and spread fingers
neurovascular: Warm pink hand, radial pulse palpable, refill <2 seconds
AIN, median, radial and ulnar nerve screens intact on documented exam
safety_red_flags: Pale or cold hand / absent refill
Increasing forearm pain or tense compartments
Median/AIN deficit, open injury or worsening swelling

learning_objective: Recognize displaced pediatric elbow fracture and prioritize perfusion, nerve assessment, safe splinting and urgent orthopedic management.

options.label: Delay urgent ischemic-limb care to obtain MRI
options.teaching_point: Ischemia needs immediate action.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Ischemia needs immediate action.

options.label: Review distal humerus AP/lateral radiographs and identify Gartland III displacement
options.teaching_point: The displaced pattern needs orthopedic involvement.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. The displaced pattern needs orthopedic involvement.

options.label: Explain and consent for surgeon-led reduction and percutaneous fixation under anesthesia
options.teaching_point: Definitive reduction and pinning belong to trained surgical team.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Definitive reduction and pinning belong to trained surgical team.

options.label: Ignore median/AIN motor examination if pulse present
options.teaching_point: Nerve damage can occur with normal perfusion.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Nerve damage can occur with normal perfusion.

options.label: Attempt pin fixation without specialist and procedural resources
options.teaching_point: Surgical procedure is not an intern task.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Surgical procedure is not an intern task.

options.label: Observe for swelling, compartment syndrome, pulse changes and escalating pain postoperatively
options.teaching_point: Continuous monitoring detects urgent complications.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Continuous monitoring detects urgent complications.

options.label: Schedule elective review in three months as only treatment
options.teaching_point: Inadequate for displaced injury.
options.when_selected_mentor: Think again: Inadequate for displaced injury.

options.label: Assess ABCs and document skin, radial pulse, hand perfusion, AIN/median/radial/ulnar nerve status and compartments
options.teaching_point: Initial full neurovascular status is time-critical.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Initial full neurovascular status is time-critical.

options.label: Order CT instead of necessary plain films and referral
options.teaching_point: Unnecessary delay.
options.when_selected_mentor: Think again: Unnecessary delay.

options.label: Give caregiver cast/pin care, return precautions and follow-up for pin removal and motion
options.teaching_point: Structured follow-up supports healing and recognizes complications.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Structured follow-up supports healing and recognizes complications.

options.label: Immobilize in a well-padded above-elbow backslab in a safe low-flexion position while displaced
options.teaching_point: Avoid excessive elbow flexion before reduction, which can worsen vascular compromise.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Avoid excessive elbow flexion before reduction, which can worsen vascular compromise.

options.label: Keep child appropriately fasted for likely procedure and coordinate pediatric anesthesia assessment
options.teaching_point: Prepare for safe operative intervention according to team instructions.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Prepare for safe operative intervention according to team instructions.

options.label: Forcefully flex swollen displaced elbow beyond 120 degrees before reduction
options.teaching_point: Could worsen vascular compromise and swelling.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Could worsen vascular compromise and swelling.

options.label: Arrange orthopedic-led closed reduction and percutaneous pin fixation with image guidance
options.teaching_point: Displaced Gartland III generally warrants specialist operative stabilization.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Displaced Gartland III generally warrants specialist operative stabilization.

options.label: Give appropriate pediatric analgesia and calmly explain plan to caregiver
options.teaching_point: Comfort and cooperation are central to safe assessment.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Comfort and cooperation are central to safe assessment.

options.label: Encourage active resisted elbow exercise before fracture fixation
options.teaching_point: Unsafe in unstable displaced injury.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Unsafe in unstable displaced injury.

options.label: Discharge in sling alone despite complete displacement
options.teaching_point: Requires urgent specialist management.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Requires urgent specialist management.

options.label: Check intraoperative alignment/pin position and document post-fixation neurovascular status
options.teaching_point: Stability and circulation are re-evaluated after fixation.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Stability and circulation are re-evaluated after fixation.

options.label: Use a tight circumferential cast over rapidly swelling elbow
options.teaching_point: Risks neurovascular compromise.
options.when_selected_mentor: Patient safety first: Risks neurovascular compromise.

options.label: Urgently contact pediatric orthopedic team and monitor perfusion continuously
options.teaching_point: Specialist evaluation is essential; ischemia changes timing to emergency.
options.when_selected_mentor: Good clinical judgment. Specialist evaluation is essential; ischemia changes timing to emergency.

stage_messages.history: Good questions uncover the mechanism and red flags. You do not need to ask everything—ask what changes your decisions.
stage_messages.examination: Slow and safe. Inspect first, localize tenderness and protect injured structures while checking nerves and circulation.
stage_messages.investigations: Choose the smallest clinically sufficient set of tests. I’ll show you each written report as you order it.
stage_messages.diagnosis: Now connect the mechanism, examination and investigations. Which diagnosis actually explains all three?

stage_messages.knowledge_check: Nice work! Three quick questions to lock in the clinical reasoning.
stage_messages.completion: Great job with Oliver! The best clinicians are careful about both decisions and patient safety.
